title: Linear Regression
subtitle: Gradient Descent & Residual Error Minimization
summary: Click on the 2D canvas to plot points and watch the best-fit line rotate into position as vertical residual error lines shrink.
intuition: Imagine placing pins on a wooden board at each data point and tying vertical rubber bands from every pin to a rigid metal rod. The rubber bands pull the rod from all directions: points far above pull it up, and points below pull it down. Where the rod naturally settles so that the total tension (squared stretch of all rubber bands) is minimized—that exact resting position is your Linear Regression line!

howItWorks.title: Initialize Slope (w) & Intercept (b)
howItWorks.detail: Start with a flat baseline line y = 0x + 0 across the 2D coordinate grid.

howItWorks.title: Compute Predictions & Vertical Residuals
howItWorks.detail: For every point (xᵢ, yᵢ), calculate ŷᵢ = w·xᵢ + b and measure the vertical dashed residual error (ŷᵢ - yᵢ).

howItWorks.title: Calculate Mean Squared Error (MSE)
howItWorks.detail: Square each residual so positive and negative errors don't cancel out, then average them: J = (1/n) Σ(ŷᵢ - yᵢ)².

howItWorks.title: Compute Partial Derivatives & Tilt Line
howItWorks.detail: Compute ∂J/∂w and ∂J/∂b to know which way to rotate the slope w and shift the intercept b.

howItWorks.title: Converge to Minimum MSE
howItWorks.detail: Repeat the update w ← w - α·∂J/∂w, b ← b - α·∂J/∂b until the residual lines shrink to their minimum.

evaluationChart.title: MSE Loss vs. Epoch Convergence
evaluationChart.description: Tracks how Mean Squared Error decays as the line rotates toward the optimal fit.

advantages: Crystal-clear interpretability: slope w directly measures Δy per unit Δx.
Convex MSE objective guarantees a single global optimum with zero local minima.
Fast O(1) inference and lightweight memory footprint.
limitations: Assumes a linear relationship; underfits curved or parabolic trends.
Sensitive to extreme outliers because residuals are squared.
Multicollinearity across correlated features destabilizes weight estimates.

formulas.label: Linear Hypothesis
formulas.description: Predicts continuous target ŷᵢ using slope w and intercept b.

formulas.label: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
formulas.description: Average squared vertical residual across all n observations.

formulas.label: Gradient Descent Update
formulas.latex: w \leftarrow w - \alpha \frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat{y}_i - y_i)x_i, \quad b \leftarrow b - \alpha \frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\hat{y}_i - y_i)
formulas.description: Updates slope and intercept opposite to the gradient.

hyperparameters.label: Learning Rate (α)
hyperparameters.description: Controls how fast the line rotates per step.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

X = np.array([1.0, 1.8, 2.5, 3.2, 4.1, 5.0, 5.8, 6.7, 7.5, 8.4])
y = np.array([2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 4.5, 4.8, 5.9, 6.2, 7.5, 7.9, 9.1])

w, b, lr, n = 0.0, 0.0, 0.02, len(X)
for epoch in range(20):
    y_hat = w * X + b
    err = y_hat - y
    dw = (2 / n) * np.dot(err, X)
    db = (2 / n) * np.sum(err)
    w -= lr * dw
    b -= lr * db
print(f'Fitted: y = {w:.4f}x + {b:.4f}, MSE = {np.mean(err**2):.4f}')
codeTemplates.production:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error

X = np.array([1.0, 1.8, 2.5, 3.2, 4.1, 5.0, 5.8, 6.7, 7.5, 8.4]).reshape(-1, 1)
y = np.array([2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 4.5, 4.8, 5.9, 6.2, 7.5, 7.9, 9.1])

model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
print(f'y = {model.coef_[0]:.4f}x + {model.intercept_:.4f}')
print('MSE:', mean_squared_error(y, model.predict(X)))

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

df = pd.DataFrame({'x': [1.0, 1.8, 2.5, 3.2, 4.1, 5.0], 'y': [2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 4.5, 4.8, 5.9]})
df = df.dropna()
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(df[['x']], df['y'], test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
print('Train shape:', X_train.shape, 'Test shape:', X_test.shape)
